t: You're at St Michael, Cornhill, a medieval parish church with a parish foundation older than the Norman Conquest. The Great Fire of London destroyed the old structure, and the present building replaced it. It's traditionally attributed to Sir Christopher Wren, while the upper parts of the tower are by Nicholas Hawksmoor. In the nineteenth century, Sir George Gilbert Scott and Herbert Williams embellished the church. Stephen Charnock, a Puritan Presbyterian clergyman who lived from 1628 to 1680, is buried here.
